summary.text: Kiernan Majerus-Collins is the Democratic candidate for the Maine House of Representatives, District 95, in the November 3, 2026 general election, in a race with no incumbent.
In a Ballotpedia survey, he described himself as an immigration and civil rights lawyer and a former member of the Lewiston School Committee.

paragraphs.text: Kiernan Majerus-Collins graduated from William Hall High School, earned a bachelor's degree from Bates College in 2018 and received a law degree from Boston University School of Law in 2024.

In a Ballotpedia survey, he said he served as a judicial law clerk to Judge Stephanie K. Seymour of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit, then returned to Lewiston to start a law practice focused on serving poor and working-class people.
Majerus-Collins won the June 9, 2026 Democratic primary with 539 votes (62.2 percent) to Matthew Kershaw's 327 (37.8 percent) and faces Republican Bret Martel in the general election.

In the Ballotpedia survey, he listed his campaign priorities as cost of living, immigrant rights and affordable housing, and said he would introduce legislation to raise the minimum wage to $20 per hour.

He also said he supports legislation barring police and jails from cooperating with federal immigration enforcement, easing construction of higher-density housing, and a constitutional amendment establishing a right to housing.
